title: Mac Mail — hourly, time cursor
description: Hourly delta ingest of ~/Library/Mail. WHERE date_received > ${CHECKPOINT_UNIX_SECONDS}; scheduler stamps ${NOW} on success. Simple, no job-side write-back. Best when the source has a reliable monotonic timestamp.

title: Mac Mail — hourly, row-id cursor (ctx.setCheckpoint)
description: Same ingest as the time variant, but cursors on max(ROWID). A groovy-map step captures the largest ROWID it saw and calls ctx.setCheckpoint(...) — the scheduler picks that up as ${CHECKPOINT} for the next run. Safer against boundary-time collisions.

title: Kafka → JVS Lucene index (continuous)
description: Long-lived Kafka consumer writing every message to a Lucene index. Runs until cancelled. NOT typically scheduled — a continuous pipeline manages its own offset (Kafka consumer group). Load this template to see the shape; you'll usually deploy it via 'Pipelines → Run' with restartable:true, not as a schedule.
